what: cost of every published quantization rung, at query time (batch 1)
runtime: @huggingface/transformers in Node (ONNX), the runtime zoteus ships
failure_note: fp16 aborts at session init on the CPU provider, with the SAME failure as nomic-768 on a different architecture: 'Attempting to get index by a name which does not exist: InsertedPrecisionFreeCast_/encoder/layer.11/output/LayerNorm/Constant_output_0 for node /embeddings/LayerNorm/Mul/SimplifiedLayerNormFusion'. nomic is a BERT variant, e5 is XLM-R; two unrelated graphs, one optimizer pass. This is an ONNX Runtime graph-optimizer defect in SimplifiedLayerNormFusion under fp16, not a model quirk. q4/q4f16/bnb4 were not swept: below the floor ratified for ticket 0240.
caveats: Latency was re-measured warm and quiet after a first cold pass; the cold pass read 731,3 / 433,3 / 397,9 MB against the warm 756,9 / 421,4 / 404,4, which brackets the measurement spread on RSS at roughly 25 MB. Read the RSS to two significant figures, not five.

One process per rung, warm cache: RSS is the total a fresh server process pays (ONNX Runtime and Node included), not the marginal cost of the weights. Loading a second model into a live process costs less, because the runtime is already there.
load_ms is warm — the weights were already downloaded. A first run also pays the download in the size column.
download_mb is the published ONNX file size on the Hugging Face repo, external data files included.
Cost, not quality. Read beside the fidelity ladder, never instead of it.
why_this_model: Zotero core's multilingual pick (spec/FIELD-REVIEW.md), and the only R7-eligible model with any evidence in this repo. Loaded from Xenova/multilingual-e5-small, not intfloat/multilingual-e5-small: the original repo publishes model_O4.onnx and model_qint8_avx512_vnni.onnx, which the transformers.js dtype knob cannot address beyond fp32.
verdict: Does NOT fit CONSTRAINTS.md C3. Its cheapest rung holds 404,4 MB resident, 1,35x the ratified 300 MB server ceiling, and no rung measured comes close. Note this is the SMALLER model of the two compared: 118M parameters and 384 dimensions against nomic-768's 137M and 768, yet 404,4 MB against nomic's 235,2 MB.
why_the_inversion: Vocabulary, not parameters. multilingual-e5-small carries 250 037 tokens against nomic's 30 528, so its embedding table is 250037 x 384 x 4 = 366,3 MB at fp32 where nomic's is 30528 x 768 x 4 = 89,4 MB. Quantization shrinks that table on disk and, on the evidence here, not in memory. Three independent quantities fit that reading: the q8 FILE at 112,6 MB is 91,6 (int8 embeddings) + ~21 (twelve quantized layers); the q8/uint8 RSS at 404-421 MB is 366,3 (embeddings back at fp32) + ~40 of runtime; and the q4 FILE at 380,2 MB is 366,3 (q4 leaves the table alone) + ~14. MECHANISM NOT PROVEN: the arithmetic is consistent with ONNX Runtime dequantizing the table for the Gather, and no direct observation of that was made. The three-way arithmetic agreement is the evidence; the cause is a hypothesis.
design_consequence: R7 and C3 may be in direct conflict, which is bigger than a model choice. Any multilingual model on a 250k-token vocabulary carries a resident floor of roughly 366 MB at 384 dimensions, and about 732 MB at 768, that quantization does not remove. If that holds, meeting 'the default embedder is multilingual' under a 300 MB ceiling needs one of: a raised ceiling, a model with a smaller vocabulary, or an engine that keeps the embedding table quantized in memory. Ticket 0240 should test the floor across candidates before comparing their quality, since a candidate that cannot fit does not need a recall number.
prefix_requirement: e5 models require 'query: ' and 'passage: ' prefixes. The model card FAQ: 'Do I need to add the prefix...? Yes, this is how the model is trained, otherwise you will see a performance degradation.' The drivers here add NO prefix. That leaves cost and dtype-vs-dtype fidelity valid, and would make any RECALL figure wrong and unfairly low against models needing no prefix. 0240's registry must carry a per-model input template.
